title: dedicated-gpu-pool-autoscale-warmup-personal-scratchpad-13
content:
Context:
- Personal scratchpad capturing commands, snippets, and hypotheses while debugging capacity thrash and warmup delays on dedicated GPU pools. Related to INFRA-3421 (users seeing long cold-starts and autoscaler oscillation during morning traffic spikes).

Observed symptom summary:
- Frequent capacity oscillation (nodes repeatedly added/removed) between 07:00-09:30 PST yesterday when daily traffic ramped from 50 qps -> 600 qps.
- Several inference pods stuck in Pending/ContainerCreating with backoff for NVidia driver init / nvidia-container-toolkit errors.
- Autoscaler bursts spawn instances that remain in STARTING for ~4-7 minutes, causing request queueing and client-side timeouts.
- When instances finally become Ready, pod warmup (model load + KV cache restore) adds 20-40s extra before serving traffic; resulting throughput lag -> autoscaler further overshoots.

Quick timeline (local notes):
- 2025-02-13T07:03:12Z: traffic spike begins (external ramp test).
- 07:05:48Z: cluster-autoscaler triggered scale-up request -> launched 3 new nodes (p4d-like).
- 07:08:13Z: 2/3 new nodes stuck in STARTING (provider vm-agent logs show integrating with internal image).
- 07:12:05Z: kubelet logs report: "failed to register node: driver mismatch" on one node.
- 07:16:32Z: first model-serving pod on new node OOMKilled while downloading artifacts to /mnt/model-cache.
- 07:24:40Z: autoscaler detects pending pods -> launches additional 4 nodes. Cycle repeats.

Commands I ran (outputs truncated):
- kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide --selector=pool=dedicated-gpu-1
  NAME                                           READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
  model-serve-abc-0                               0/1     ContainerCreating   0          3m    pending

- kubectl describe pod model-serve-abc-0 -n serving
  Events:
    Normal  Scheduled  2m  default-scheduler  Successfully assigned serving/model-serve-abc-0 to ip-10-0-3-45
    Warning FailedAttachVolume  2m kubelet  AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "model-cache" : rpc error: code = Internal desc = device mount failed
    Warning FailedCreatePodSandBox 1m kubelet  Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to setup network for sandbox

- journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | grep -i nvidia
  Feb 13 07:10:05 ip-10-0-3-45 kubelet[1234]: E02013 07:10:05.123 k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/kubelet: failed to register GPU device plugin: timeout connecting to /var/lib/nvidia/driver.sock

- kubectl logs node-provisioner-xyz -n infra --since=30m
  2025-02-13T07:06:44Z INFO launching vm instance id i-0abc1234
  2025-02-13T07:08:19Z WARN instance i-0abc1234 reported status STARTING longer than expected (4m)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Node-level driver/AMI mismatch: new nodes boot with an AMI that has older/newer Nvidia drivers than the runtime expects -> node GPU plugin fails and kubelet marks GPUs unavailable -> pods stay pending. Evidence: kubelet logs about driver socket timeout. Some nodes show "driver mismatch" messages.
2) Model artifact download contention: multiple pods try to download large model (10-30GB) into shared EBS/PD model-cache causing I/O stalls; some pods OOM or stuck at ContainerCreating while waiting for mount. Evidence: OOMKilled during artifact download; AttachVolume failures.
3) Autoscaler overshoot due to delayed warmup: we treat Pending pods as unmet demand; autoscaler keeps adding nodes while existing new nodes are still provisioning + model warmup, causing oscillation. Evidence: scale-up events while earlier nodes still not Ready; long model load times documented (~20-40s) on fresh nodes.
4) Prepull/cold cache policy not aggressive enough: cache prewarming does not populate KV caches or model weights before routing traffic leading to throughput cliffs even after nodes Ready. Evidence: serving logs show first requests hitting model load path with heavy CPU/GPU spikes.

Things I tried (and notes):
- Quick repro: ramp test in staging cluster (traffic generator) -> reproduced similar pattern.
- Confirmed AMI & driver: SSH into problematic node, checked /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and nvidia-smi version. Found mismatch between kernel module version and driver binary on 2 nodes.
  commands: uname -r; nvidia-smi --query; rpm -qa | grep nvidia
  result: kernel module 530.x, binary 535.x -> potential incompatibility.

- Workaround applied to staging: temporarily pinned autoscaler max surge to +3, limited scale-up rate; created a pre-warmed pool of 4 spare nodes in dedicated-gpu-1 (manual reserve) -> reduced oscillation but not eliminated.

- Tried prepull hook: created DaemonSet to prefetch model into local cache on nodes as they become Ready (simple curl to model store). This reduced first-request time on fresh nodes from ~35s -> ~12s, but still not enough during extreme ramp. Side effect: heavy network egress when many nodes spool downloads simultaneously.

- Adjusted scheduler priority: moved critical-serving pods to a higher priorityclass so they preempt less-critical workloads; helped reduce pending time but didn't fix driver/socket issues.

Logs & snippets (copied):
- kubelet error:
  E0213 07:12:05.441  kubelet.go:205] failed to register node: runtime error: invalid device plugin response: expected 0 GPUs but device plugin reported 4

- pod init container log:
  2025-02-13T07:15:24Z init: downloading shard 3/6 -> 4.2GB at 50MB/s
  2025-02-13T07:15:54Z init: extraction succeeded
  2025-02-13T07:16:12Z init: start model mmap -> OOMKilled

Immediate mitigations considered / applied:
- Add pre-warmed spare node pool (manual) for peak hours -> worked as a short-term mitigation. Needs automation + cost accounting.
- Harden AMI build: ensure driver/kernel alignment; add smoke check on boot to assert nvidia-smi responsive before marking node for traffic.
- Stagger automated artifact prefetching (jitter) to avoid stampeding downloads.
- Improve autoscaler logic: consider warmup-aware scale-up (do not count Pending pods alone; prefer metrics like ReadyCapacityRamp or a learned warmup model).

Open action items / next steps (tracking):
- [ ] INFRA-3421: add AMI driver compatibility test in release pipeline (owner: Samir)
- [ ] Create automated pre-warm job with exponential backoff/jitter to avoid thundering herd (owner: Taylor)
- [ ] PR: serving-runtime#986 (investigate preseed caches + model load instrumentation) -> follow up on perf numbers (Aisha)
- [ ] Add kubelet boot probe to node bootstrap that fails fast if GPU plugin cannot register within 45s -> prevents autoscaler from counting partially-healthy nodes (owner: infra/release-engineering)

Questions / unresolved:
- Why some nodes show "expected 0 GPUs but device plugin reported 4"? Could be kubelet/node-alloc mismatch on labeling or a race during driver init. Need to reproduce with kernel-driver pair in lab.
- Would using a smaller model shard size (more shards) improve overlapping downloads vs memory pressure? Need cluster-level IO tests.

Notes to self (commands to run in lab):
- Build a test AMI with driver 535 and kernel x.y, then intentionally vary driver to reproduce plugin failure.
- Run workload with N=50 model pulls concurrent, measure time-to-first-response with/without prewarm.
- Instrument our autoscaler to emit 'scale-intent' vs 'intended-ready-capacity' metrics so we can detect overshoot.

Slack/thread refs:
- See thread in #infra-dedicated-gpu: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/CGPU12345/p1708601234012345

If I get cycles tomorrow: try to reproduce driver socket timeout locally with minikube + device-plugin mock; also sanity-check our model-store bandwidth shaping options.

End of scratchpad.
